name: Super Game Boy
description: A Super NES / Super Famicom cartridge adapter from 1994 that plays Game Boy games on a television. It contains its own Game Boy processor and adds colour palettes and decorative borders, with some games offering enhanced graphics and sound.

specs.cpu: Game Boy CPU (Sharp LR35902 core) @ ~4.295 MHz (NTSC)
specs.memory: 8 KB RAM / 8 KB VRAM (Game Boy side)
specs.graphics: Game Boy LCD image, 160×144, recoloured by the SNES with borders
specs.sound: Game Boy APU, mixed through the SNES

curiosities: Because its clock is derived from the SNES, games run about 2.4% faster than on a real Game Boy on NTSC systems.
The Japan-only Super Game Boy 2 (1998) fixed the speed and added a link cable port.
Space Invaders contains a full SNES version of the game that is copied into the console's RAM and run when played on a Super Game Boy.
Built-in menus let players pick from 32 colour palettes or paint their own border.
story: Nintendo wanted Game Boy owners to play on the television too: the Super Game Boy, released in 1994, was a Super NES cartridge with a Game Boy inside it and a slot on top for Game Boy cartridges.

It added colour palettes, a border round the picture and, in games made for it, special colours, borders and sound from the Super NES. Donkey Kong '94, Kirby's Dream Land 2 and the first Pokémon games took advantage of it.
A Super Game Boy 2 with a link port followed in Japan in 1998, and the idea came back as the Game Boy Player for the GameCube.
